title: Hybrid commitment scenarios and warm-standby runbook — Lyra pilot
content:
Context:
This doc captures the proposed dedicated-capacity commitment scenarios and an operational runbook for a hybrid reserved+autoscale deployment tailored to Customer Lyra's pilot. Goal is to give a concrete, conservative recommendation that balances 99th percentile latency SLOs, cost predictability, and graceful degradation during peaks. These numbers are based on microbenchmarks run on our staging cluster (quantized 13B variant) on 2025-10-30 and lightweight synthetic traffic that approximates Lyra's expected prompt distribution.

Customer profile (as discussed in kickoff):
- Primary workload: user-facing chat + summarization in product UX.
- Avg requests/day: 150k (projected in pilot month) with diurnal peak factor ~3x
- Typical input length: 120 tokens; typical output length: 380 tokens -> ~500 tokens total per request
- Target SLO: 99th <= 300ms tail for initial pilot (soft), 95th <= 200ms for baseline interactive routes
- Traffic split: 70% short-turn chat (<= 128 out tokens), 30% long summaries (>= 512 out tokens)
- Feature flags: LRU prefix caching available for repeat prompts; model variant: quantized 13B (fp16->int8) in production path

Empirical perf numbers used (staging, median of 10 runs):
- H100-80GB (quantized 13B)
  - avg throughput: 9 requests/sec for 500-token requests (p95 latency ~220ms when concurrency capped)
  - steady qps with kv-cache hits: +40% effective throughput for repeated prompts
- A100-80GB (older gen): ~6 requests/sec for same payload (p95 ~310ms under load)
- L4 (inference-optimized small): 22 requests/sec for 128-token payloads (not suitable for long summaries)

Cloud cost assumptions (all-in hourly cost including reserved discount estimates):
- H100-80GB reserved unit price (committed) estimate: $28/hr (committed reserved pricing used for scenarios)
- A100-80GB committed estimate: $20/hr
- L4 spot/ephemeral: $2.8/hr (good for short-chat offload)
- On-demand autoscale penalty (cold-start + orchestration overhead): assume 10–15% extra effective cost per hour when autoscaled from zero (due to prewarmed bursts / GPU startups)

Sizing approach and assumptions:
- We size to cover 95th expected peak qps with reserved capacity and rely on autoscale to handle spikes beyond that.
- Warm-standby fraction: maintain N_prewarm GPUs kept on (but not fully utilized) to avoid cold-starts for the most latency-sensitive routes.
- For long-tail summary requests, prefer routing to H100 pool with prewarmed cache; for short chat, prefer L4 or A100 depending on price/quality tradeoff.

Scenario calculations (rounded):
- Peak QPS target (pilot): baseline 50 qps average -> diurnal peak 150 qps; conservatively plan for 200 qps for burst safety margin.
- Throughput projections (500-token average request):
  - H100: 9 req/sec per GPU -> need 23 GPUs to sustain 200 qps (200/9 = 22.2)
  - A100: 6 req/sec per GPU -> need 34 GPUs to sustain 200 qps
  - Mixed: allocate long-summary load (30% of traffic -> 60 qps) to H100; short-chat (140 qps) to L4/A100 layer: 60 qps / 9 =~ 7 H100 GPUs + 140 qps / 22 (L4 for smaller requests) ~= 7 L4-equivalent GPUs -> but L4 can't handle summaries so plan explicit split below.

Three recommended commitment scenarios (conservative to aggressive):
1) Conservative (lowest risk, higher cost):
   - Reserved: 24 H100 GPUs (covers 200 qps with minimal autoscale)
   - Warm-standby: keep all 24 on with 75% target utilization to keep 99p latency low
   - Autoscale: spike pool allowed up to +12 GPUs (on-demand) with cooldown 90s, step +4 GPUs
   - Monthly committed cost (H100): 24 * $28/hr * 730h = $490,560
   - Pros: meets SLOs with headroom; minimal runtime surprises
   - Cons: highest monthly bill for pilot; less efficient if traffic much lower than forecast

2) Balanced (recommended for most pilots):
   - Reserved: 10 H100 + 8 L4 (for chat short flows)
   - Warm-standby: keep 6 H100 prewarmed for long summaries (rotation policy to avoid GPU hot-dust)
   - Autoscale: allow +14 H100 ephemeral (preemptible/on-demand) and +6 L4; scale steps: +3 GPUs every 45s, cooldown 60s
   - Routing policy: route top-20% heaviest/longest requests to H100 pool; short chat to L4 with fallback to H100 when L4 is saturated
   - Monthly committed cost: H100: 10 * $28 * 730 = $204,400; L4: 8 * $2.8 * 730 = $16,352 -> total ~ $220.7k/month
   - Expected typical utilization: 40–65% with autoscale smoothing; cost-effective for mixed load

3) Lean (lowest commit, autoscale-heavy):
   - Reserved: 4 H100 (critical paths only) + 4 L4
   - Warm-standby: 2 H100 prewarmed, 2 L4 prewarmed
   - Autoscale: aggressive up to +40 H100 with elastic autoscaler using spot instances for bulk; prewarming via burst-queueing when predicted traffic > threshold
   - Monthly committed cost baseline: H100: 4 * $28 * 730 = $81,760; L4: 4 * $2.8 * 730 = $8,176 -> baseline ~ $89.9k/month + autoscale on-demand costs
   - Pros: lowest committed spend; good if Lyra values cash flow over latency predictability
   - Cons: 99th latency SLO risk during large bursts; more operational complexity

Warm-standby and prewarm strategy (runbook items):
- Maintain a small group of GPUs that are always live (prewarm set). For Balanced scenario: 6 H100 kept in warm-standby with ephemeral KV-cache primed to known prompt families.
- Rotation / utilization policy: rotate warm-standby GPUs weekly to avoid thermal throttling and even out GPU wear.
- Cache priming: run a scheduled job each 10 minutes that pushes top-100 frequent prefixes into KV cache on warm GPUs (script in infra repo PR #452).
- Health checks: active synthetic requests every 30s to check p95 latency and KV hit rates. If p95 > SLO, trigger autoscale-by-policy.

Autoscaler configuration (concrete settings for Balanced scenario):
- Scale target metric: queue depth + p95 latency (composite) with priority to queue depth for throughput
- Min: reserved_count - prewarm_count (so reserved GPUs are not torn down below warm set)
- Max: reserved_count + 14 (caps ephemeral grow)
- Scale step up: +3 GPUs per 45s; step down: -2 GPUs per 120s (longer cooldown to avoid oscillation)
- Prewarm threshold: predicted QPS > 0.7 * reserved_capacity for two consecutive 60s windows -> prewarm +2 GPUs
- Fallback policy: if autoscale cannot provision within 90s and queue depth > threshold, degrade long-summary routes to a smaller model (A/B via routing policy) or return a low-resolution summary version.

Operational playbook for pilot start (first 30 days):
- Week 0 (pre-launch): provision Balanced scenario reserved pool (10 H100 + 8 L4), deploy route rules, and run golden traffic replay against warm pool. Validate p95 on synthetic sets.
- Day 1–3: enable canary traffic (5–10% of production), watch queue depth, p95, token-cost. Tune autoscale cooldowns if oscillation observed.
- Day 4–14: ramp to 50–75% traffic; capture cost telemetry; enable KV cache priming for top 200 prompts.
- Day 15–30: full ramp to 100% pilot traffic; evaluate whether reserved count should move +/- 2 GPUs based on sustained utilization and cost curve.

Risks and mitigations:
- Rapid, sustained burst > reserved + autoscale cap: mitigation = automatic degrade to a smaller model variant for non-critical routes + region fallback.
- Spot eviction when relying on preemptible autoscale: mitigation = maintain a small guaranteed pool and prefer regions with lower preemption rates; stagger spot requests.
- Cold-start tail: mitigation = aggressive warm-standby and prewarmed KV cache for top N prefixes; rollback to smaller model on timeouts.

Open questions for Lyra and engineering:
- Confirm acceptable graceful-degradation modes (shorter summary vs truncated content) and UX signal to users when degraded.
- Agree on committed budget envelope for pilot month and threshold for auto-escalation to enterprise sales.
- Confirm whether Lyra wants per-token cost reporting surfaced in Console during pilot (we can enable token-level breakdown but requires retention setting change).

Action items (owners in parens):
- Finalize traffic shape + sample logs from Lyra (Lyra product) (Jonah Park)
- Schedule region/instance preference check with infra (Ravi Kapoor)
- Wire Confluence runbook into alerting playbooks (Elena Novak)
- Merge KV-cache priming job: infra PR #452 review and deploy (Asha)

Appendix: quick math note (Balanced scenario):
- 200 qps total, split 30% summaries (60 qps) -> 60/9 ~= 7 H100 GPUs to cover long requests
- Short chat 140 qps -> map to L4: 140/22 ~= 6.4 -> round up 7 L4-equivalent
- We chose 10 H100 (more headroom) + 8 L4 (slightly more chat capacity and to account for imperfect routing) to reduce autoscale churn and keep p95 latency within SLO while enabling cost-savings vs full H100-only fleet.

Notes/References:
- Benchmark logs: infra/perf/lyra-2025-10-30 -> see PR #452 for raw numbers
- Related runbooks: reserved-pool-dimensioning-workshop-aurora-poc-notes.json (for heuristics)
- Slack thread summary: C12345, pinned messages

End of document.
